Project: Kubernetes. Upgrade being assessed: 1.23 -> 1.29.
This change was introduced in release *. Source: Kubernetes Version Skew Policy (official_api_docs). Section: Supported version skew / kube-proxy.
Version facts from package metadata for this release (authoritative for version numbers): none

ITEM:
<<<
kube-proxy may be up to three minor versions older or newer than the kubelet instance it runs alongside (kube-proxy < 1.25 may only be up to two minor versions older or newer than the kubelet instance it runs alongside).
>>>

PARENT CONTEXT (same section, for disambiguation only):
<<<
Supported version skew / kube-proxy: kube-proxy must not be newer than kube-apiserver. kube-proxy may be up to three minor versions older than kube-apiserver (kube-proxy < 1.25 may only be up to two minor versions older than kube-apiserver). kube-proxy may be up to three minor versions older or newer than the kubelet instance it runs alongside (kube-proxy < 1.25 may only be up to two minor versions older or newer than the kubelet instance it runs alongside). Example: kube-apiserver is at {{< skew currentVersion >}} kube-proxy is supported at {{< skew currentVersion >}}, {{< skew currentVersionAddMinor -1 >}}, {{< skew currentVersionAddMinor -2 >}}, and {{< skew currentVersionAddMinor -3 >}} {{< note >}} If version skew exists between kube-apiserver instances in an HA cluster, this narrows the allowed kube-proxy versions. {{</ note >}} Example: kube-apiserver instances are at {{< skew currentVersion >}} and {{< skew currentVersionAddMinor -1 >}} kube-proxy is supported at {{< skew currentVersionAddMinor -1 >}}, {{< skew currentVersionAddMinor -2 >}}, and {{< skew currentVersionAddMinor -3 >}} ({{< skew currentVersion >}} is not supported because that would be newer than the kube-apiserver instance at version {{< skew currentVersionAddMinor -1 >}})
>>>

Decide the disposition:
- "risk": the item describes something that can break an app/deployment, require migration work, or create operational risk.
- "context": it is accurate but needs no action at 1.29 (no user action required, deprecated-but-working, additive feature). Give the reason.

For "risk", produce one or more risk paths. Use separate paths for separate symbols/APIs when they can be checked independently. Hard rules:
1. Every condition has at least one quote copied EXACTLY, character for character, from ITEM or PARENT CONTEXT (contiguous span, 3-40 words, no ellipses, no added words). Do not fix typos or formatting.
2. Each path has exactly one condition with category "version" stating that the upgrade crosses release * (quote the text that ties the change to this release, or the change statement itself), and at least one application/deployment condition (category api_usage, configuration, dependency, runtime, deployment, database, behavior or test_coverage) describing what the app or deployment must use/have for the risk to apply.
3. If the text does not state something you need, do not assert it: use role "uncertain" and explain in ambiguities. derived_by: "extraction" when the text states the fact; for an application/deployment condition ("the application uses X"), use "extraction" when the text names X as the thing affected by the change. Use "inference" only when you infer an affected symbol, scope or impact that the text does not name. Only add ambiguities for real gaps or conflicts in the text, not for the general fact that a specific application has not been inspected.
4. role: "required" (must hold), "alternative" (any one of the alternatives suffices), "optional" (raises impact), "disqualifying" (if it holds, the risk does NOT apply, e.g. not using the new opt-in API), "uncertain".
5. operator/expected_value must be checkable: e.g. operator "present" with expected_value the literal symbol; "less_than" with a version; "equals" with a setting value. expected_value is a string.
6. If a replacement API/setting/version is named, put the migration step in suggested_actions and add a condition for any behavior that differs in the replacement when the text states one.
7. search_queries: for app-side conditions with a literal symbol, give ripgrep regexes (tool "ripgrep"), kubectl commands (tool "kubectl") or SQL (tool "sql") that would find usage. Empty list if no literal symbol.
8. primary_symbol: the most specific identifier of the change (full apiVersion string like "policy/v1beta1", setting name, function, flag, or runtime name like "Python"/"Node.js"). symbols: all identifiers involved.
9. risk_level rubric: critical = upgrade fails or data is at risk for most users meeting the conditions (e.g. unsupported runtime/database version, removed API version that stops serving); high = code or config meeting the conditions breaks at upgrade; medium = behavior change or migration with a clear workaround; low = edge case, cosmetic, or warning-only.
10. fires_at: "upgrade" (at upgrade time), "first_use" (when a feature is first exercised), "rotation" (on credential/password rotation), "rollout" (on deployment rollout), "future_removal" (deprecated now, removed later).
11. applies_to: fill upgrade_method (e.g. "pg_upgrade", "dump/restore"), cluster_type, or from_versions (a version specifier like "<3.1") ONLY if the text restricts applicability; otherwise null.
Do not output confidence.

paths.path_name: kube-proxy and kubelet minor-version skew during 1.23 to 1.29 upgrade
paths.description: During an upgrade from 1.23 to 1.29, kube-proxy and the kubelet on the same node can end up more than three minor versions apart, which the stated skew policy does not allow.

conditions.statement: The upgrade moves the cluster from 1.23 to 1.29, a span of six minor versions, and the change statement applies to this upgrade.
quotes: kube-proxy may be up to three minor versions older or newer than the kubelet instance it runs alongside
conditions.relevance: Establishes the allowed kube-proxy to kubelet minor-version window that the 1.23 to 1.29 upgrade may exceed.
ambiguities: The text does not name the release tied to this change, so it does not confirm the change applies to the 1.23 to 1.29 upgrade.

conditions.statement: kube-proxy and kubelet run at minor versions more than three apart on the same node.
quotes: kube-proxy may be up to three minor versions older or newer than the kubelet instance it runs alongside
conditions.relevance: A minor-version gap above three between kube-proxy and kubelet violates the stated skew window.

suggested_actions: Compare the kubelet version on each node with the kube-proxy image version.
Upgrade kube-proxy and kubelet so that the minor-version gap stays within the stated window at every step of the upgrade.

paths.path_name: kube-proxy newer than kube-apiserver during upgrade
paths.description: If kube-proxy is upgraded ahead of kube-apiserver, kube-proxy becomes newer than kube-apiserver, which the stated skew policy does not allow.

conditions.statement: The upgrade moves the cluster from 1.23 to 1.29, and the change statement applies to this upgrade.
quotes: kube-proxy must not be newer than kube-apiserver
conditions.relevance: Sets the rule that kube-proxy must not be newer than kube-apiserver, which the 1.23 to 1.29 upgrade may violate.
ambiguities: The text does not name the release tied to this change, so it does not confirm the change applies to the 1.23 to 1.29 upgrade.

conditions.statement: kube-proxy is running at a newer minor version than kube-apiserver.
quotes: kube-proxy must not be newer than kube-apiserver
conditions.relevance: A kube-proxy version newer than kube-apiserver violates the stated skew rule.

suggested_actions: Upgrade kube-apiserver before kube-proxy so that kube-proxy is never newer than kube-apiserver.
